newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes consolidate at weak levels, sours gain.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes consolidate at weak levels, sours gain.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes retreated Monday in a consolidation move after last week's price spike, while sour grade differentials continued to benefit from pipeline spill at Texaco's Eugene Island facility.
June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing leveled around 60 cents lower at $21.45-55 a barrel.
June/July WTI spreads extended a rapid fallout, currently talking at 38 cents in favor of July, and pushing June Postings Plus to the $1.80-85 level from $2.05 on Friday.
NYMEX June futures contracts expire at the close of business Tuesday, helping to keep June/July rolls uneven and volatile, traders said.
Late Friday, Texaco said its 176,000 barrels per day (bpd) Eugene Island pipeline was shut after a split in the pipeline caused a spill into Lake Barre in Louisiana.
About 20,000 bpd of the crude has been diverted to the Poseidon pipeline system, also owned by Texaco.
Cash traders were left wondering if force majeure declarations would be in the offing, since the amount of lost crude was significant, and repairs still underway.
"You're talking about 500,000 to one million barrels total lost production," said a Texas trader, assuming the pipeline returns to service by a tentative restart date on Thursday.
Grade trades have seen Eugene Island sour barrels dealt at $1.45 and $1.40 under June WTI/Cushing, 15-20 cents stronger than late talk on Friday.
West Texas Sour/Midland received a slight edge from the Eugene Island supply concerns, selling at $1.40 and $1.38 discounts, roughly even to a few pennies firmer.
Sweet Louisiana barrels turned weaker Monday, selling for Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James at discounts of three, five and seven cents.
Brent-WTI spreads have come in considerably, putting arbitrage numbers closer to $1.40 in favor of WTI from a more than $1.75 edge late last week.
June/July Brent spreads have remained stuck around plus 1-3 cents, allowing declining June WTI to close the gap, and make it less economical for trans-Atlantic shipments.
Physical Brent barrels gained strength, with a cargo of June 3-5 crude sold at July Brent -20 cents to a U.S. trader.
